haiku-low.q1: It gets a 401 Unauthorized. No rate-limit counter is read or changed.
haiku-low.q2: 100 requests per minute in total for Standard. All of a customer's API keys share one per-customer budget.
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After value in seconds. The request is never forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. A rejected request leaves the counter unchanged, so 429s use no budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The count is incremented before forwarding and never rolled back, so the request stays counted.
haiku-low.q6: Fail open: the request is forwarded, metric ratelimit_store_unavailable is emitted, and no X-RateLimit headers are added. No retry.
haiku-low.q7: Standard is 100 requests per minute. Enterprise limit is open (ENTERPRISE_LIMIT = TBD); Enterprise is unlimited and skips the check until set.
haiku-low.q8: In one shared Redis, under key rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}. Each key expires after 120 seconds.
haiku-low.q9: The count restarts at zero at each new clock minute, since windows are fixed. Old keys expire after 120 seconds. A full Redis loss resets current windows.
haiku-low.q10: The check is one atomic Redis Lua script that reads and increments only if below the limit. Redis runs scripts one at a time, so two instances cannot both take the last slot.
haiku-low.q11: Retry-After is 60 minus (now mod 60), minimum 1, using the Redis clock. For example, a rejection at 12:00:42 gives 18.
haiku-low.q12: No retry. The client gets the backend response with no X-RateLimit headers.

sonnet.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized. No rate-limit counter is read or changed.
sonnet.q2: Only one shared budget: the counter is per customer, so all of a customer's keys share it (the plan limit per minute, e.g. 100 for Standard). Up to 2x the limit is possible across a minute boundary.
sonnet.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header (seconds). The backend never sees the request; it is not forwarded.
sonnet.q4: No. The script leaves the counter unchanged on rejection, so 429s use no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The count is incremented before forwarding and never rolled back, so it stays used even when the backend fails.
sonnet.q6: Fail open: the request is forwarded to the backend, the metric ratelimit_store_unavailable is emitted, and no X-RateLimit headers are added.
sonnet.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: not decided (ENTERPRISE_LIMIT = TBD, owned by Product); until set, Enterprise customers are treated as unlimited and skip the check.
sonnet.q8: In the shared Redis (primary with replica), under key rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}, where windowStart is epoch seconds divided by 60. Each key expires after 120 s.
sonnet.q9: It resets automatically when the next clock minute starts (fixed window); the count starts at zero in each new minute.
sonnet.q10: The gateway makes a single call to Redis that runs a Lua script, which checks the count and increments it only if below the limit. Redis runs scripts one at a time (atomically), so two instances cannot both take the last slot.
sonnet.q11: Whole seconds until the window ends: 60 - (now mod 60), minimum 1, using the Redis clock (the script's time). Example: rejected at 12:00:42 gives 18.
sonnet.q12: No retry, because a retry would exceed the 50 ms budget. The client gets no X-RateLimit headers (no rate-limit info).
